label: Person
name: Abraham Viruthakulangara
summary:
Abraham Viruthakulangara (1922–1992) was an Indian Catholic Archbishop of Nagpur and one of the significant leaders of the Catholic Church in central India during the post-independence period. Born in Kerala — the heartland of Indian Catholicism — he was ordained a priest and eventually appointed Archbishop of Nagpur, a diocese serving one of India's most religiously diverse regions.

Viruthakulangara's archiepiscopate at Nagpur coincided with the post-Vatican II period of Catholic renewal and the rapid development of the Indian Catholic Church's indigenous character. Nagpur itself is a city of significant religious diversity and the geographic centre of India, serving communities that include Hindu, Buddhist, Muslim, and Christian populations. The Buddhist revival movement centred on B.R. Ambedkar had significant presence in the Nagpur region.

His ministry engaged the social challenges of central India — tribal communities, dalit populations, poverty, and the social transformation of India's independence period. As President of the Catholic Bishops' Conference of India (CBCI), he contributed to the national Catholic Church's collective governance and its engagement with Indian society, government, and inter-religious dialogue.
